subject: Private edge: latency attribution addendum request
messages:
From: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@hearthline.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@hearthline.com, legal@hearthline.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment latency attribution — request for addendum

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough on Thursday. We are excited to move forward with Redwood Private in our GCP colo, but our security and network teams raised a concern: the private link and edge peering for our site introduce variable egress latency originating inside our managed network.

To meet our corporate compliance and our internal SLO reporting, we need an explicit contract addendum that:
- Clarifies that latency caused by customer-managed edge devices, NAT gateways, or third-party transit providers is excluded from Redwood uptime/latency obligations,
- Defines an evidence and telemetry exchange process (PCAPs, BGP metrics, packet loss windows) so we can jointly adjudicate incidents, and
- Establishes an operational fallback (canary to hosted model or degraded throughput) when private path latency exceeds thresholds.

I've attached a simple network diagram and flagged the peering points. Can Redwood propose language we can share with our legal team? Procurement would like a draft SLA addendum today if possible — we have a vendor review meeting next Friday.

Thanks,
Alicia Moreno
VP IT Operations, Hearthline Therapeutics
(attachment: Hearthline_Network_Diagram.png)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@hearthline.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment latency attribution — request for addendum

Hi Alicia — appreciate the clear ask and diagram. High-level response: we can accommodate a customer-controlled-network latency carveout, but we need a few concrete items to make it operational and contract-ready:

1) A responsibility matrix that enumerates the boundary devices/configs you control (edge routers, NATs, on-prem WAN).
2) A mutually agreed incident evidence protocol (timestamps, traceroutes, tcpdump sample windows, any BGP visibility).
3) A fallback policy that specifies when Redwood will fail over to hosted model instances and what the expected latency/cost trade-offs are.

I looped in Vanessa (network reliability) and Priyom (solutions/legal) to draft language and the evidence exchange flow. We should be able to get a DRAFT addendum back to you within 48 hours. Is your legal team available for a quick sync on Monday to confirm evidence requirements?

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@hearthline.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 10:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment latency attribution — request for addendum

Hi all — quick technical note from ops: the carveout needs to be specific about three measurable dimensions so we can automate incident attribution:

- Path ownership: list of IP prefixes and ASN ranges that are customer-controlled. If the forwarding path includes hops in those ranges, we tag the trace as "customer-side".
- Observable signals: packet loss > 1% sustained for 30s, RTT delta > 150ms vs. baseline for 1m, SYN retransmits above threshold.
- Evidence windows: shared pcap or aggregated flow logs for a 5-minute window around the incident, with UTC timestamps and sequence numbers.

I've attached a short template (SLA_Addendum_DRAFT.pdf) with suggested contract text and a sample incident evidence checklist. We can support automated collection hooks (sflow/netflow) if you can provide a collector endpoint and auth.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Network Reliability
Redwood Inference
(attachment: SLA_Addendum_DRAFT.pdf)
From: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@hearthline.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@hearthline.com, legal@hearthline.com
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment latency attribution — request for addendum

Thanks Vanessa — that template looks useful. A few quick items from our side:
- We can supply prefix lists and ASN ranges by COB Tuesday.
- Legal requested that the carveout include an "escalation play" where Redwood provides a one-week mitigation window (configuration guidance + temporary traffic steering suggestions) before the exclusion applies to uptime calculations.
- Procurement wants the addendum to include service credit language if Redwood's fallback to hosted instances is not available within the mitigation window.

Can Priyom confirm whether the proposed evidence phrasing will be contract-ready, and if the mitigation window language is acceptable? Alicia (legal) will be on the call Monday at 10:00 PT.

— Alicia
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@hearthline.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 11:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment latency attribution — request for addendum

Hi Alicia — thanks for the responses and for scheduling the call. Summary of legal/contract stance:

- We can add an explicit "Customer-managed network latency exclusion" with three clauses: definitions (ownership boundaries), evidence exchange process, and mitigation/mitigation-failure remedies.
- The mitigation window you requested (7 days) is reasonable if we include a phased mitigation requirement (Day 0–2: diagnosis and recommended config; Day 3–5: assist with temporary traffic steering; Day 6–7: fallback to hosted instances). If Redwood cannot provide fallback capacity within that window for reasons on Redwood's side, we will accept an SLA credit ladder (0.5% credit for first missed SLA objective, 1.5% for second, etc.).
- We will not accept open-ended "customer accepts all risk" language. The addendum must preserve Redwood's obligation to attempt remediation and provide evidence for attribution decisions.

I've uploaded a redlined clause set and a DocuSign starter link for execution. Please review: https://docusign.com/embedded?doc=HL-2028-07-Edge-01

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Counsel
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@hearthline.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Jul 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment latency attribution — request for addendum

Alicia — thanks for the productive week. Next steps and commitments from Redwood:

1) We will deliver the FINAL addendum (attached SLA_Addendum_FINAL.pdf) into your procurement queue today and share the DocuSign starter in parallel.
2) Ops will provision a small canary pool in us-west-2 to be used as the fallback for the first 30 days post-cutover; we will also publish threshold alerts and an automated traceroute collection endpoint.
3) Legal confirms the 7-day mitigation window and the credit ladder; the addendum preserves Redwood's remediation obligations and the evidence exchange protocol.

Please confirm procurement will route the DocuSign to contracts by EOD Monday to keep the original timeline. If you want, we can run a joint dry-run of the traceroute / evidence exchange next Thursday.

— Karthik
(attachment: SLA_Addendum_FINAL.pdf)
